AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
items.excerpt: A new real-world test puts AI coding agents in a simulated developer job with colleagues, project boards, and incomplete handoffs, where they have to keep developing software on their own and reliably close open tickets in a messy daily workflow. Even Opus 5.5 and Astra fall far short, solving fewer than one in ten tasks completely. The models finish clear, standalone assignments quickly, but they lose track as autonomous developers. The article AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog
items.excerpt: Perplexity is launching a Monitor API that searches the web on a schedule and alerts agents via webhook only when relevant changes occur. Its own decision model filters out unimportant results. For Perplexity, the API is part of a broader strategy to stand out from an increasingly interchangeable chatbot business through developer tools. The article Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns
items.excerpt: METR reports that leading AI models like Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are improving rapidly at research tasks but getting harder to measure. Current data can't rule out a dangerous acceleration in AI development, the organization warns, though it also says common tests may overestimate what the models can actually do. items.title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
items.excerpt: Security researchers at Dragos used two million fake AI requests to uncover serious vulnerabilities in the AI supply chain, finding at least three compromised providers, hundreds of stolen AWS keys, and marketplace resellers who were simply reading customer requests. OpenRouter responded by removing three providers and 125 endpoints. items.title: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
items.excerpt: The Lean and Mathlib community has officially confirmed Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis as correct. Dozens of independent verifiers checked the 17 million lines of computer code. The solution arrived years earlier than expected: Terence Tao had predicted it wouldn't happen until around 2050 and didn't expect AI to solve it alone. items.title: A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels
items.excerpt: TensorLean, from Columbia University and CertiK, formally verifies production GPU kernels at the PTX level using Lean. It checked 149 kernel instances, proved 83 correct, and found 38 bugs in FlashAttention, DeepGEMM and more.
